title: A systematic review of AI literacy scales
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of a comprehensive, quality-focused overview of instruments used to measure AI literacy. The author reviews existing AI literacy scales to determine how well they assess constructs such as understanding AI, using AI, evaluating AI, and AI ethics, and to judge which instruments are most suitable for different research and educational contexts.

The review systematically searched Scopus and arXiv, plus reference lists and citation searches, to identify studies that developed or revalidated AI literacy scales. Twenty-two studies validating or revalidating 16 scales were included. The scales covered several populations, including secondary school students, higher education students, general adults, and teachers; most were self-report Likert scales, while a smaller number were performance-based tests. The review used COSMIN and GRADE criteria to assess content validity, structural validity, internal consistency, reliability, construct validity, responsiveness, interpretability, and feasibility.

The main conclusion is that AI literacy measurement is still an emerging field with uneven psychometric quality. The scales generally showed strong structural validity and internal consistency, but content validity, reliability, responsiveness, and interpretability were often weak or unreported. No scale had evidence for cross-cultural validity or measurement error. The paper concludes with recommendations for choosing instruments by target population and for future work to improve validation, cross-cultural testing, and transparency.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI chatbot or large language model system used for conversational text generation, question answering, and related assistance without a specific named product identified.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper did not evaluate a generative AI tool directly; it is a systematic review of AI literacy scales, with one included instrument addressing perceptions of generative AI and ChatGPT literacy as part of AI literacy measurement.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of measurement scales, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool’s effect on outcomes. It does not report a treatment-comparison design or outcome effects for a generative AI intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: No intervention effect sizes or outcome impacts are reported for a generative AI tool. The paper focuses on scale quality and measurement properties rather than student outcome change.
